Item 1. Business

Our business operates two product segments serving enterprise customers. The segments share engineering resources but face different competitors and customer purchasing cycles.

Customer concentration remains significant. Diversification of products does not guarantee diversification of demand, and losing a major customer could reduce sales.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

Our supply chain depends on a limited number of manufacturers. Interruptions could delay customer deliveries and reduce revenue even if demand remains stable.

We maintain alternative supplier arrangements. However, qualification of a replacement supplier may take several quarters and may not offset an immediate disruption.

Item 2. Properties

Offices and leased facilities.

Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

Management attributes revenue growth to stronger enterprise demand and a favorable product mix. Operating margin improved as fixed costs were spread over higher sales.

However, management does not expect all of these benefits to recur. Higher capital spending and slower collections could reduce cash flow despite reported revenue growth.

Liquidity is supported by operating cash flow and existing cash balances. The capital allocation plan prioritizes capacity investment before incremental shareholder distributions.

Item 9A. Controls and Procedures

Management evaluated internal control over financial reporting and concluded that controls were effective. This conclusion reflects management's assessment at the fiscal year end.

The audit committee oversees the financial reporting process. Its oversight does not eliminate the possibility of errors or future changes in the effectiveness of controls.
